name: Order of the Mare
source: WEB, Grade 2a warband, converted from mordheimer.net (/docs/warbands/grade-2a-warbands/order-of-the-mare) on 2026-10-10.

heroSlots.notes: Weapons/Armour: The Paragon may be equipped from the Footman equipment list.

specialRules.name: Leader
specialRules.description: Any warrior within 6” of the Questing knight may use his Leadership value when taking Leadership tests.

specialRules.name: Knight’s virtue
specialRules.description: The Paragon follows the rules of Knight’s virtue.

specialRules.name: Vow of poverty
specialRules.description: The Paragon may not use a Lance.

heroSlots.notes: Weapons/Armour: The Dame of the Mare comes equipped with an ancient armour that may never be removed, traded or stolen. It does not prevent spell casting, and provides a 5+ save that cannot be modified, but doesn’t work against magical attacks. She may otherwise be equipped from the Dame equipment list.

specialRules.name: Prayers
specialRules.description: The Dame of the Mare may use prayers from the Blessings of the Mare list. She starts with one randomly determined prayer.

heroSlots.notes: Weapons/Armour: The Gallant may be equipped from the Footman equipment list.

specialRules.name: Knight’s virtue
specialRules.description: The Gallant follows the rules of Knight’s virtue.

heroSlots.notes: Weapons/Armour: Squires may be equipped from the Archer equipment list.

henchmenTypes.notes: Weapons/Armour: Pilgrims may be equipped from the Footman equipment list.

specialRules.name: Hatred
specialRules.description: Pilgrims are so devout to the Dame of the Mare that they hate all and any enemies that defy her.

specialRules.name: Peasants
specialRules.description: While devout and loyal, pilgrims are simple peasants with no ambition other than following their chosen saint, as such may never become heroes. Reroll any The Lad’s Got Talent results.

henchmenTypes.notes: Weapons/Armour: Bowmen may be equipped from the Archer equipment list.
Weapons/Armour: Redeemed knights may be equipped from the Footman equipment list.

specialRules.name: Knight’s virtue
specialRules.description: Redeemed knights follow the rules of Knight’s virtue.

henchmenTypes.notes: Weapons/Armour: The Filly fights with its hooves, and suffers no penalty for fighting unarmed. It is clad in odd-looking covering like were they from bygone times, yet it shimmers with a spectral gleam. The covering provides the beast with a 5+ save that cannot be modified, but doesn’t work against magical attacks. The filly may never take any equipment, except for the covering it already carries.

specialRules.name: Horse
specialRules.description: The filly is an animal and thus does not gain any experience. Additionally it follows the movement rules for mounted warriors.

specialRules: Knight’s virtue: A knight is a chivalrous warrior who is superior to ordinary warriors. He will never panic and break from combat and so does not have to pass a Leadership test for being all alone. | Hired swords: Order of the Mare warbands have access to the same hired swords as a mercenary warband would. | Horse and rider: Because the knights of Bretonnia are typically mounted on horseback, the Paragon and the Gallant may buy a single horse or warhorse each at half the normal price upon recruitment.
background: From the woodlands of eastern Bretonnia, and from every village and town within a day’s ride from the Forest of Loren, echoes the rumours of the Mare witch. A crone of the dark arts according to some, but revered as the Prophetess of the Mare to her increasing number of followers. Claiming to be the heir of ancient heroes from the days of Gilles Le Breton, she sees it her right to restore honour to once-shunned knights. Eager to restore their honour the knights swear allegiance to her, as they once did to their former lords or even the Lady of the Lake. The latter, known now as Paragons, are given a new purpose by the Prophetess of the Mare, leading them on a quest for wyrdstones in Mordheim. Journeying alongside the Paragons on their hunt for the curious artefacts are a unique gathering of warriors known as the Dames of the Mare. | The Prophetess appoints these Dames to her retinues, each possessing peculiar powers that some might label as witchcraft. Despite their unconventional abilities, the Paragons, beguiled by the Mare Witch, overlook the mystical nature of their allies. Despite the Bretonnian tradition, typically distrustful of such magic, the knights are so entranced by the noble and inspiring Dames of the Mare that they willingly dismiss such reservations. | A distinctive practice among the Dames involves the premature elevation of promising squires. These young warriors, granted extraordinary strength and courage, become knights errant and form a crucial bond with the Paragons whom they join on their long journey to the City of the Damned. In an unexpected turn, the Dames replace the elevated squires with young girls, initiating them into the mysterious order of the Dames of the Mare.
